rubric.criterion: material fidelity to the art bible
rubric.note: Walnut: the shared basecolor texture is on target (mean L* 30.7, #683E25), but the lit top renders lighter and redder than oiled walnut #583C26 (L* 28.0, C* 20.7, hab 62.9). Measured: p5-dice-ingame-d6-tray box (384,768)-(717,896) #81533D L* 39.9 C* 26.8 hab 51.2, dE 14.1. xr-emu-15 left eye (120,700)-(280,780) L* 39.3, dE 14.3. engine-player-view (100,300)-(250,360) #7B4027 L* 33.9 C* 35.0 hab 48.2, dE 17.0. It reads as cherry or mahogany. The grain is soft and painterly (texture period 85 px per 1024 tile, about 4 cm), which fits the bible. Brass sits in the same mean family as the automatons, but it is flat. Gear in p5 (1160,412)-(1225,446): L* 51.1, p95 56.5. Golem fist in xr-emu-12 (540,480)-(610,540): L* 43.6, p95 74.8. Gear vs #DEC16A dE 38.9. The tray and rim use brass-aged (normal mean tilt 26.9 deg), which draws a concentric ring and scratch swirl, so the brass reads like gilded end-grain wood (crop p5 (820,760)-(1720,1000)). Felt is factor-only (GLB felt baseColorFactor 0.102/0.005/0.009, no map, no sheen). Its high-pass SD is 0.29 in xr-emu-15 (340,830)-(510,895) and 0.56 in engine-player-view (300,395)-(500,450), against walnut 5.77 and 8.18, so it reads as flat paint, not cloth. Felt colour #6F2825 L* 26.8 is darker than ruby #93212B (dE 16.4).

Both states have clean, readable silhouettes. Unfolded is a 1.50 x 0.80 m oval on a walnut barrel apron and a brass bell foot (engine-unfolded 240-600 x 215-480). Folded is a drop-leaf: the leaves hang to y 0.367 m (report.json), and their D-shaped skirts read clearly in engine-folded 250-555 x 205-470. Both depart from Paul's pick, table-sheet-1. That sheet shows a brass-banded drum when folded and radial walnut petals around exposed gearing when unfolded. Its panel 3 shows a velvet tray recessed into the top with a bevelled brass frame. The asset has a raised open box sitting on the planks instead (tray outer walls stand about 30 px tall in p5 at 2560 px wide). The barrel apron with brass bands is the only carry-over of the drum language.

With the hero probe (xr-emu frames, p5, AgX), the table sits warm and coherent. Under the same lights it is about twice as bright as the study wood: table top L* 39.9 vs bookcase side L* 34.2 in p5 (1830,360)-(1900,380), door L* 19.9 in xr-emu-12 (690,250)-(780,450), ceiling beam L* 20.4 in xr-emu-15 (390,0)-(420,35). So it pops as separately lit. The brief's weighted in-fight shot, p3-desktop-fight-1-table (dated 2026-11-15, capsule enemies), renders all brass black: gear (592,525)-(612,545) L* 0.1, back rim (560,459)-(720,466) L* 5.7, pad frames black. This is runtime: metallic brass with no env map. main.ts reflect() only binds heroEnv when it exists. The staging engine shots show the same effect at oblique angles: tray rim L* 14.0 in engine-unfolded (318,270)-(410,283), 6.6 on the grazing tray side. Baked AO (atlas mean 0.605 over the covered area) does not show at contacts. Next to the tray the top is lighter, not darker: p5 +5.2 L* left of the tray, -3.1 below it, engine-player-view +2.9 and +2.3. three.js aoMap only darkens indirect light, so this is a runtime fault, not a bake fault.

Dice read well. The d6 (1318,612)-(1398,700) in p5 is dE 31.7 against the felt and 25.3 against the back inner tray wall. Cards on walnut: ruby dE 30.4, sapphire 65.1, emerald 54.1. Weak spots: a ruby attack card on the ruby felt pads is only dE 16.4. The draw and discard pads are small (about 150 x 60 px in the 2560 px p5 frame). In p3 the tray is lost under the fanned hand and the black brass frames merge with the black rim. Felt vs walnut is dE 19.8, and the top is uncluttered apart from the central gear plate.

No gap, step or grain break shows at the leaf hinges (x = +/-0.4 m) in 4x and 2x crops of engine-player-view (100,280)-(300,600), xr-emu-15 (140,630)-(340,900) and p5 (300,380)-(900,1050). The hinge lines sit inside the plank grooves, and report.json says unfolded_top_flush true. Defects: the brass-aged normal draws a concentric swirl centred on the tray's front face and along the front rim band (p5 rim (300,1060)-(700,1090) L* SD 13.1). At grazing light the walnut normal turns bark-like: engine-grazing (580,300)-(760,440) L* SD 16.7, against 4.0 in the top-down view, which edges toward the photographic grime the bible rules out. AO is missing at contacts, as noted under lighting.

Present: three small brass hinge knuckles per leaf, visible when folded (4x crop of engine-folded (420,245)-(545,300)), a brass rim band, brass-framed felt pads, a gear plate with a domed boss, a banded barrel apron, and a bell foot. Missing compared with table-sheet-1 panel 3: brass strap inlays between the panels, the brass flourishes, the bevelled recessed tray and the sunk card well. The plank grooves are the only top detail. Edges are hard with no visible bevel highlight on the tray (tray rim front L* SD 3.1 in p5).

topFixes: Recess the dice tray into the top with a bevelled brass frame, and add brass strap inlays between the top panels, per table-sheet-1 panel 3 (scripts/assets/build-combat-table.py)
Always give the table brass an environment probe: fall back to a RoomEnvironment PMREM when heroEnv is null (src/main.ts reflect() and the table load). In p3 the gear renders at L* 0.1

Bring the table walnut down toward #583C26 (rendered L* 39.9, hab 51 -> about L* 30, hab 60) with a walnut slot tint in bindTableMaterials (src/combat/table-asset-proof.ts), or by lowering the light over the table, so it matches the study wood
Make the felt read as cloth: add a nap normal or detail texture and a sheen (MeshPhysicalMaterial sheen), and lift it toward ruby #93212B (the felt slot in the build script and bindTableMaterials)

Fix the brass-aged swirl on the tray walls and rim band: re-UV those faces or switch them to brass-polished at a lower normalScale (brass-aged normal tilt 26.9 deg), and drop roughness so highlights reach the automaton p95 of about L* 75
Make contact shadow visible under the tray, gear plate and pads: bake the AO into the base colour or a lightmap, or add a contact-shadow decal, because aoMap only darkens indirect light
independentScore.method: I read docs/art-bible.md and the concept Paul picked (assets-source/concepts/table-sheet-1.png). The tone, brightness and contrast verdicts are weighted to the in-fight frames, which use the shipping AgX tone mapping (src/main.ts:108): the xr-emu fight frames (6, 12 to 16, 21, 22, chosen from a contact sheet) and p5-dice-ingame-d6-tray.jpg as the clearest in-game study frame with a die on the felt. p3-desktop-fight-1-table.jpg and p3-desktop-fight-2-dice.jpg were judged as the desktop path. The four staging engine-*.jpg shots (form, folded state, grazing light) were judged next, while noting that table-asset-proof renders them with its own RoomEnvironment probe at 0.45. The review sheet, report.json and the GLB and manifest were used only to attribute faults to bake or runtime. With Pillow and numpy (python3 -I, scripts in /tmp/fb17/table-score/scripts/), I measured box-region mean sRGB, CIE L*, C*, hue angle, HSV saturation, L* SD and p05/p95. I also measured high-pass SD (luminance minus a 3 px Gaussian blur) for cloth versus wood, CIE76 dE between surfaces and palette hexes, and contact-strip L* next to vs 30 px away from the tray and gear. The shared textures were measured too: walnut basecolor mean, an FFT grain period, normal-map mean tilt, and AO atlas coverage. I made 2 to 4x crops of every scored area (annotated boxes and crops in /tmp/fb17/table-score/crops/), and read the binding and env code in src/combat/table-asset-proof.ts and src/main.ts. The study desk renders (engine.desk.png, desk.lightmapped.png) are too dark to read: desk L* 2.5 to 6.3. So the study comparison uses the room wood in the same xr-emu and p5 frames (door, beam, bench, bookcase, wainscot).
